title: speq environment v1
description: One file in the environments directory, selected with --env. Read by read_env_config in speq-cli/src/cli/run.rs, which treats 'baseUrl', 'headers' and 'http' specially and turns every other top-level key into a variable of the same name. This schema is therefore open, unlike the other .speq schemas. Any string value may carry an '${VAR}' placeholder, resolved from the OS environment when the file is loaded; '${VAR:-default}' supplies a fallback and '$${VAR}' is a literal. Substitution happens before this schema applies, so a placeholder is never itself validated against the field's type.

baseUrl.description: Prefix for relative step URLs. Also exposed as the variable {{baseUrl}}. Defaults to an empty string, which requires every step to use an absolute URL.

name.description: Conventional label for the environment. The CLI does not read it — like any other key it simply becomes the variable {{name}}. The environment is selected by filename, not by this field.

headers.description: Headers sent with every request of the run. Values are template-rendered like a step's headers, so they may reference environment variables. A step's own 'headers' entry of the same name replaces the environment one, case-insensitively, so only one spelling reaches the wire. Unlike every other key, this one does not become a variable.

http.description: Transport policy narrowing the manifest's 'http' block for this environment. Merged field by field: fields left unset here keep the manifest's value. Like 'headers', this key does not become a variable.

additionalProperties.description: Any other key becomes a variable of that name, referenced as {{key}}. Values may be any JSON value.
